## RTMB

- Take base R code, compile into C++ and build a tape
- Code running in C++ is generally faster than in R
- The tape is the computation of the 'chain rule' to compute gradients
- Each computation within the tape that doesn't change is pre-computed
- Taped derivative is called automatic differentiation and it gives numerical gradients with analytical precision

## The Tape

- Consider a Poisson distribution 

$$
\begin{align}
  l(\lambda|x) & = x\log(\lambda) - \log(x!) - \lambda
\end{align}
$$

```{r}
#| echo: true

library(RTMB)
x <- 3
f <- function(lambda) x*log(lambda) - lfactorial(x) - lambda
fc <- MakeTape(f, 2)
fc$print()
```

## Gradients in RTMB

$$
  \frac{dl}{d\lambda} = \frac{x}{\lambda} - 1.
$$

```{r}
#| echo: true

fc$jacobian(1)
x/1-1
fc$print()
```

## RTMB Sockeye Ricker

```{r}
#| echo: false
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
sox <- read.csv("../data/sockeye/SRDATA2026 1.csv")
stock <- read.csv("../data/sockeye/FC_StockInfo 2.csv")
sox <- sox %>% left_join(stock, by = "PopID")
sox <- sox %>% filter(!is.na(spawners), !is.na(recruits))
sox <- sox %>% group_by(PopName) %>% mutate(sd_spawners = sd(spawners),  spawners_scaled = spawners/sd_spawners) %>% ungroup()
```

```{r}
#| echo: true

sox$stock <- as.numeric(factor(sox$PopName))
nstocks <- max(sox$stock)
parameters <- list(
  alpha = runif(nstocks, 2, 5),
  logbeta = runif(nstocks, 0, 1),
  logsigma = runif(nstocks, 3, 5)
)

sox$logRS <- log(sox$recruits/sox$spawners)

negll <- function(pars){
  getAll(pars)
  beta <- exp(logbeta)
  sigma <- exp(logsigma)
  mu <- alpha[sox$stock] - beta[sox$stock]*sox$spawners_scaled
  -sum(dnorm(sox$logRS, mu, sigma[sox$stock], log = TRUE))
}
obj <- MakeADFun(negll, parameters, silent = TRUE)
```


## RTMB Speed Up

```{r}
#| echo: true

microbenchmark::microbenchmark(
  "R" = negll(parameters),
  "RTMB" = obj$fn(obj$par)
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: true

count <- 0
negll_vec <- \(pars){
  params <- obj$env$parList(pars)
  count <<- count + 1
  negll(params)
}
gr <- numDeriv::jacobian(negll_vec, obj$par)
print(count)

microbenchmark::microbenchmark(
  "R" = numDeriv::jacobian(negll_vec, obj$par),
  "RTMB" = obj$gr(obj$par),
  times = 10
)
```

## RTMB Hessian

- Finite differences approximate the gradient by evaluating function nearby and computing slope.
- Requires multiple function evaluations for each parameter
- Hessian requires even more evaluations with additional numerical error
- Accurate and fast Hessian required for standard errors

## Reporting Parameter Values

- `REPORT` to return value of variable
- `ADREPORT` to include uncertainty of variable
- `sdeport` will return standard deviations of parameters

```{r}
#| echo: true

negll <- function(pars){
  getAll(pars)
  beta <- exp(logbeta)
  sigma <- exp(logsigma)
  beta_real <- beta*sox$spawners/sox$sd_spawners
  ADREPORT(beta_real)
  mu <- alpha[sox$stock] - beta[sox$stock]*sox$spawners_scaled
  -sum(dnorm(sox$logRS, mu, sigma[sox$stock], log = TRUE))
}
obj <- MakeADFun(negll, parameters, silent = TRUE)
fit <- nlminb(obj$par, obj$fn, obj$gr)
sdr <- sdreport(obj, fit$par)
summary(sdr, "fixed")[1:5,]
summary(sdr, "report")[1:5,]
```
